We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-3}\frac{3}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-3}\frac{3}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}]}_{a}^{-3} \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }[-\frac{1}{(-3)^{3}}+\frac{1}{{a}^{3}}] \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{27}+\frac{1}{{a}^{3}}) \\  & =(\frac{1}{27}+0) \\  & =\frac{1}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$
